propositions: Phase 3 proposers read identical evidence and their agreement measures prompt stability rather than correctness, creating a convergence validation gap
Phase 2 verification scores findings for validity but does not validate that remediations name a concrete triggering input that produces the asserted harm
Phase 3 proposals can reverse deliberate recorded project decisions without surfacing the prior decision record or evidence that conditions have changed since the decision

The five-phase pipeline needs harm_reachable as a fifth validity sub-question and prior_decision as an intent check, both integrated into Phase 2 scoring, to close the validation gap before Phase 4 approval

Phase 3 remediation must differentiate proposer inputs asymmetrically and resolve divergence through targeted research comparing community and project records, emitting converged, research-resolved, or no-consensus moves
Plan items must surface prior_decision records and HARDENING reclassifications at Phase 4 approval so the reviewer is never shown hardening work presented as a bug or reversals without justification
